lessons.title: Choose the product and write a specification
prerequisites: Complete the web foundations or know how to open the project, edit a file, and verify the result in a browser. No previous commercial experience is required.
objectives: Turn Choose the product and write a specification into concrete, measurable decisions that can be applied to a real store.
Turn an unambiguous sourcing product specification into concrete, measurable decisions that can be applied to a real store.

Turn Define dimensions, materials, tolerances, colors, packaging, marking, tests, quantity, destination, and unacceptable defects before requesting price. into concrete, measurable decisions that can be applied to a real store.

blocks.text: Define dimensions, materials, tolerances, colors, packaging, marking, tests, quantity, destination, and unacceptable defects before requesting price. A sound decision always connects the customer need, the visual or commercial rule, its implementation in the site, and an observable signal. This prevents vague preferences and copied tactics whose purpose is not understood.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Choose the product and write a specification is like arranging a physical shop: every color, space, message, or offer should help a visitor understand where they are, what they can buy, and why they can trust the next step.

Define dimensions, materials, tolerances, colors, packaging, marking, tests, quantity, destination, and unacceptable defects before requesting price. Name the precise problem before selecting a tool. Observe context, device, intent, and customer objections. Then write a hypothesis that links one change to an expected result without presenting that hypothesis as established fact.

To master Choose the product and write a specification, first build a minimal version with explicit rules, then inspect it on mobile and desktop. Contrast normal, empty, long, and error cases. Quality comes from a coherent testable system, not from accumulating visual effects or promotional messages.

This lesson delivers an unambiguous sourcing product specification. It must record the starting situation, decision, expected evidence, and safety limit. Compare behavior and before/after metrics over enough time while accounting for traffic, costs, and satisfaction.

blocks.text: Match entity, beneficiary, and invoice; put specifications, tolerances, inspection, date, remedy, and Incoterm in the protected order; reject unverified bank changes. A sound decision always connects the customer need, the visual or commercial rule, its implementation in the site, and an observable signal. This prevents vague preferences and copied tactics whose purpose is not understood.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Contract, Trade Assurance, payment, and fraud prevention is like arranging a physical shop: every color, space, message, or offer should help a visitor understand where they are, what they can buy, and why they can trust the next step.

Match entity, beneficiary, and invoice; put specifications, tolerances, inspection, date, remedy, and Incoterm in the protected order; reject unverified bank changes. Name the precise problem before selecting a tool. Observe context, device, intent, and customer objections. Then write a hypothesis that links one change to an expected result without presenting that hypothesis as established fact.

To master Contract, Trade Assurance, payment, and fraud prevention, first build a minimal version with explicit rules, then inspect it on mobile and desktop. Contrast normal, empty, long, and error cases. Quality comes from a coherent testable system, not from accumulating visual effects or promotional messages.

This lesson delivers an order and payment checklist with stop gates. It must record the starting situation, decision, expected evidence, and safety limit. Compare behavior and before/after metrics over enough time while accounting for traffic, costs, and satisfaction.
